tagline: Over the Colorado, under the cliffs, across the mountain lying down.
intro: From Bitter Springs US 89A runs north along the foot of the Echo Cliffs, past bead stands and hogans, then turns west across the Colorado on Navajo Bridge and leaves Navajo land for the Arizona Strip. From there it follows the base of the Vermilion Cliffs, a 3,000-foot escarpment, past old trading post buildings at Soap Creek built around standing hoodoos, and out into the ranchland of House Rock Valley.

Then the road climbs steep and winding onto the Kaibab Plateau, which the Paiute called the mountain lying down, tops 7,900 feet, and comes down the far side to Fredonia, a name said to mean land of free women.

moments.title: Navajo Bridge
moments.text: Traffic takes the 1995 span. The original bridge beside it, which replaced the ferry at Lees Ferry, is kept for walking out 467 feet above the river.

moments.title: House Rock Valley
moments.text: A side road runs north under the cliffs to the California condor release site, where the reintroduction began in 1996. Traces of the Mormon Honeymoon Trail follow the fence.

moments.title: Jacob Lake
moments.text: The road crests at an inn founded in 1923 for tourists trying to reach the Grand Canyon. SR 67, the only paved road to the North Rim, starts here.

sources.label: ADOT, Fredonia-Vermilion Cliffs Scenic Road Corridor Management Plan (Wayback Machine snapshot)
